description: This topic explores the meaning and types of families, the functions and roles of family members, their rights and responsibilities, the importance of a good family, and the challenges families face along with possible solutions.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best describes a family?

options.text: A group of strangers living in the same town
A group of people related by blood, marriage or adoption who live together
A group of workers in the same office
A group of pupils in the same class

mcq.explanation: A family is a basic social unit made up of people connected by blood, marriage or adoption, who normally live together and care for one another.

mcq.questionText: A family that consists of a father, a mother and their children only is called a:

options.text: Extended family
Single-parent family
Nuclear family
Polygamous family

mcq.explanation: A nuclear family is made up of parents and their own children only, without other relatives.

mcq.questionText: Which type of family includes grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins living together with parents and children?

options.text: Nuclear family
Extended family
Single-parent family
Foster family

mcq.explanation: An extended family includes close relatives beyond the parents and children, such as grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins.

mcq.questionText: A household headed by only a mother or only a father raising children alone is known as a:

options.text: Nuclear family
Extended family
Single-parent family
Joint family

mcq.explanation: A single-parent family is one in which a child or children are raised by one parent only, due to reasons such as death, divorce or separation.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a major function of the family?

options.text: Collecting government taxes
Bringing up and socialising children
Printing money for the country
Building national roads

mcq.explanation: One of the most important functions of the family is to raise children and teach them values, norms and acceptable behaviour through socialisation.

mcq.questionText: The process by which children learn the language, customs and values of their society mainly through the family is called:

options.text: Industrialisation
Urbanisation
Socialisation
Globalisation

mcq.explanation: Socialisation is the lifelong process of learning a society's culture and norms, and the family is the first and most important agent of socialisation.

mcq.questionText: Which one is a responsibility of children in a family?

options.text: Paying school fees for their parents
Obeying parents and helping with household chores
Providing shelter for the whole family
Employing the parents

mcq.explanation: Children have the responsibility of respecting and obeying their parents and assisting with reasonable household duties.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a basic right of every child within a family?

options.text: The right to be neglected
The right to education and good health care
The right to refuse all family rules
The right to leave school for work

mcq.explanation: Every child has the right to basic needs such as education, health care, food, shelter and protection from harm.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a key role of parents in the family?

options.text: Providing basic needs and guidance to children
Forcing children into early marriage
Denying children the chance to play
Encouraging children to drop out of school

mcq.explanation: Parents are responsible for providing food, shelter, clothing, education and moral guidance to their children.

mcq.questionText: Why is a good family important to the development of a nation?

options.text: Because it produces responsible and disciplined citizens
Because it increases the number of criminals
Because it reduces the population to zero
Because it stops people from working

mcq.explanation: A good family raises well-behaved, responsible citizens who contribute positively to the development of the nation.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a common challenge facing many families today?

options.text: Too much peace and unity
Poverty and shortage of basic needs
Having too much love among members
Excellent communication between members

mcq.explanation: Poverty makes it difficult for families to meet basic needs such as food, education and health care, and is a major challenge.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a suitable solution to conflicts within a family?

options.text: Ignoring all family members
Using dialogue and peaceful discussion
Using violence to settle disputes
Running away from home

mcq.explanation: Conflicts in a family are best solved through dialogue, tolerance and peaceful discussion among members.

mcq.questionText: The family is often described as the basic unit of society because:

options.text: It is where new members of society are born and raised
It is the largest organisation in the world
It collects taxes for the government
It controls the national army

mcq.explanation: The family is the smallest and most basic unit of society, where children are born, nurtured and prepared to join the wider community.

mcq.questionText: An economic function of the family is:

options.text: Printing currency notes
Providing food, clothing and other basic needs to members
Setting national interest rates
Managing the stock market

mcq.explanation: The economic function of the family involves working to provide and share basic needs such as food, clothing and shelter among members.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best shows good cooperation in a family?

options.text: Members sharing duties and helping one another
Each member living independently with no contact
Parents ignoring the needs of children
Children refusing to do any work

mcq.explanation: Good cooperation is shown when family members share responsibilities, support each other and work together for the good of all.

fib.questionText: A _____ family is made up of a father, mother and their children only.
fib.explanation: A nuclear family consists only of parents and their own children.

fib.questionText: A family that includes grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins together with parents and children is called an _____ family.
fib.explanation: An extended family includes close relatives beyond the parents and children.

fib.questionText: When a child is raised by only one parent, that family is known as a _____ family.
fib.explanation: A single-parent family has one parent raising the children alone.

fib.questionText: The family is regarded as the basic _____ of society.
fib.explanation: The family is the smallest and most basic unit that makes up the wider society.

fib.questionText: The process through which children learn the values and norms of their society is called _____.
fib.explanation: Socialisation is the process of learning a society's culture, and the family is its first agent.

fib.questionText: Providing food, shelter and clothing to family members is an example of the _____ function of the family.
fib.explanation: The economic function involves meeting the material and basic needs of the family.

fib.questionText: One of the major responsibilities of children is to _____ their parents.
fib.explanation: Children are expected to respect and obey their parents and elders.

fib.questionText: Every child in a family has the right to _____, which prepares them for a better future.
fib.explanation: Education is a basic right of every child and helps prepare them for adult life.

fib.questionText: _____ is a common family challenge that makes it hard to meet basic needs such as food and school fees.
fib.explanation: Poverty limits a family's ability to provide for the basic needs of its members.

fib.questionText: Family conflicts are best solved through peaceful _____ among members.
fib.explanation: Dialogue and discussion help members understand one another and settle disputes peacefully.

tf.questionText: A nuclear family is made up of parents and their children only.
tf.explanation: A nuclear family includes only the father, mother and their own children.

tf.questionText: An extended family includes only the husband and wife with no children.
tf.explanation: An extended family is larger and includes relatives such as grandparents, uncles and aunts in addition to parents and children.

tf.questionText: The family is the first agent of socialisation for a child.
tf.explanation: Children first learn language, values and behaviour from their family before any other group.

tf.questionText: Children have no responsibilities in the family.
tf.explanation: Children have responsibilities such as obeying parents, respecting elders and helping with household chores.

tf.questionText: A single-parent family can result from the death, divorce or separation of one parent.
tf.explanation: Single-parent families often arise when one parent is absent due to death, divorce or separation.

tf.questionText: Poverty is one of the challenges that can affect the well-being of a family.
tf.explanation: Poverty makes it difficult for families to meet basic needs and is a serious challenge.

tf.questionText: Violence is the best way to solve disagreements in a family.
tf.explanation: Disagreements should be solved through dialogue and tolerance, not violence.

tf.questionText: Providing basic needs and guidance to children is a role of parents.
tf.explanation: Parents are responsible for meeting children's basic needs and guiding their upbringing.

tf.questionText: A good family contributes to the development of a peaceful and responsible society.
tf.explanation: Good families raise responsible citizens who help build a peaceful and developed society.

tf.questionText: Only the government, and not the family, is responsible for teaching children good values.
tf.explanation: The family plays the leading role in teaching children good values and acceptable behaviour.

summary.correctAnswer: A group of people related by blood, marriage or adoption who live together and care for one another.
summary.explanation: The family is the basic social unit of society.

summary.correctAnswer: Nuclear family, extended family and single-parent family.
summary.explanation: These are the common types of families studied at Form 1 level.

summary.correctAnswer: A family made up of a father, mother and their children only.
summary.explanation: It is the smallest type of family with no other relatives.

summary.correctAnswer: A family that includes parents, children and other relatives such as grandparents, uncles and aunts.
summary.explanation: It is larger and includes members beyond the nuclear family.

summary.correctAnswer: A family in which children are raised by one parent only.
summary.explanation: It may result from death, divorce or separation of a parent.

summary.correctAnswer: Reproduction, raising and socialising children, and providing basic needs.
summary.explanation: The family ensures the survival and proper upbringing of its members.

summary.correctAnswer: Obeying and respecting parents, helping with chores and studying hard.
summary.explanation: Children contribute to the family by behaving well and assisting at home.

summary.correctAnswer: The right to food, shelter, education, health care and protection.
summary.explanation: Each member, especially children, is entitled to basic needs and protection.

summary.correctAnswer: It raises responsible citizens and builds a peaceful, developed society.
summary.explanation: Good families form the foundation of a strong nation.

summary.correctAnswer: Challenges include poverty and conflicts; solutions include hard work, cooperation and dialogue.
summary.explanation: Working together and communicating peacefully help families overcome challenges.

hoq.questionText: In a rural village, the Mwita household lives with the parents, their children, the grandmother and two cousins, all sharing duties and resources. Which type of family is this and what is one main advantage of it?

options.text: Nuclear family, because it offers privacy
Extended family, because members share responsibilities and support one another
Single-parent family, because one parent is absent
Nuclear family, because it has the fewest members

hoq.explanation: Because relatives such as grandparents and cousins live together with parents and children, this is an extended family, whose strength is shared responsibility and mutual support.

hoq.questionText: A child in a certain family is denied schooling and forced to work all day at home. Which combination best explains what is happening?

options.text: The child's right to education is being violated and family responsibilities are being misused
The child is enjoying the right to play and rest
The family is correctly performing its socialisation function
The child is being given the right to education

hoq.explanation: Denying a child education and overloading them with labour violates the child's right to education and misuses the idea of family responsibilities.

hoq.questionText: Two families face the same problem of low income. Family A members argue and blame each other, while Family B members discuss the problem and plan a small business together. What does this difference mainly show?

options.text: That poverty cannot be solved in any family
That cooperation and dialogue help a family overcome challenges better than conflict
That arguing is the best way to solve family problems
That income has no effect on family life

hoq.explanation: The example shows that families that cooperate and use dialogue are better able to overcome challenges such as low income than families that quarrel.
